reasons.reader_question: Kiran bolting mid-sentence leaves a sharp question, though readers mostly know the answer, so the real pull is how Meera learns.
reasons.change: Ila raises Rohan's personal stakes, a costed deal is struck, a bound promise is made, and Kiran flees the house.
reasons.romance_movement: Their first goal clash as lovers is settled by an equal trade, each giving up something real. The beat lands.
reasons.shown_chemistry: The open hands, the hum and the count entry work. 'Odd light, as if it pleased her' narrates the attraction.
reasons.character_logic: Rohan sees Kiran's scarred ear bare after reading the ear-rim report (F063). He looks foolish or the reveal comes early.
reasons.stakes_and_cost: Half-treated children against his sister and the seal. Both costs are said aloud, and the promise binds him to the cold.
reasons.prose: Mostly clean and concrete. 'Winter had come in October' breaks the winters calendar, and several lines are stiff or wrong.
reasons.continuity: The day count conflicts: four days at ch19 minus a day slept is not 'four days', and the road arithmetic fails.

fixes: At 'four days till the Fair and a day and a half of road': continuity conflict. F178 gave four days at ch19's close, and Kiran has since slept a full day, so three remain. Recount everything: Fair three days off, Rohan concedes one day, the marked cases' last dose at tomorrow's dusk, leave the next dawn, a day and a half of road lands them the evening before the Fair. Update the 'second day' scene, the patrol's third-day line and F185/F187/F189.

At 'the white scar of his ear bare': Rohan's POV sees the ear while he knows the report's frozen ear-rim (F063). Either he looks foolish (technique 13 failure) or the reveal jumps ahead of ch29. Keep the wool cap on as Kiran runs, or let Meera block the doorway, so Rohan sees only stockings on frozen mud and the open lane.

At 'Winter had come in October': a real month in a world that counts winters breaks the texture. Write 'Winter had come a month early.' Also fix 'She had put her own name into a book' (she wrote his name, not hers; say 'She had written the worst of me into her book'). Replace 'as if it pleased her to be treated so' with a visible action, such as her capping the ink and sitting forward.
reader_question: Why did Kiran run the moment Rohan asked whose rope Dilan was on, and what will Meera do when she catches him?
new_facts_assessment: F185/F187 rewrite the beat (six days to four, three to two). This could work, but the dates clash with F178 after Kiran's day of sleep, and the arrival maths fails. F189 applies F149 well and adds a useful cost.
